title: Two settings pages disagree about whether a filter wheel exists; per-filter adaptive-exposure limits become unreachable
what_happened: With the Simulated Filter Wheel connected (log: 'Simulator connected: id=sim_filterwheel_1 type=FilterWheel', 15:04:48), Settings > Equipment > Autofocus > 'Autofocus Filter Settings' lists 7 filters (L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII), while Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure > 'Per-filter overrides' shows a warning banner 'No filter wheel on active profile - adaptive applies to every capture (mono camera assumption).' The per-filter min/max/enable editor is replaced by that banner, so per-filter adaptive limits cannot be configured at all.
expected: Both pages read the same source of truth. If a filter wheel is connected with named filters, Adaptive Exposure must offer the per-filter editor for those filters (or at minimum say 'no equipment profile saved' rather than asserting there is no filter wheel).
repro: Fresh profile, Skip onboarding. Equipment > 'I'll do it manually' > Discovery Expand > Filter Wheels > Connect (Simulated Filter Wheel). Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure > enable 'Enable global default' -> banner says no filter wheel. Settings > Equipment > Autofocus, scroll to 'Autofocus Filter Settings' -> 7 filters listed.
proposed_fix: Make the adaptive-exposure per-filter editor fall back to filterWheelStateProvider.filterNames when the active profile has none (same precedence the Autofocus page uses), and reword the banner to name the real cause ('No filter wheel connected and no filters on the active profile').
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on display :82, profile settings-imaging-verify, fresh. Connected Simulated Filter Wheel (app.log 15:14:27 'Simulator connected: id=sim_filterwheel_1 type=FilterWheel'). Settings > Equipment > Autofocus > Autofocus Filter Settings lists 7 rows L/R/G/B/Ha/OIII/SII (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-16-af-scroll.png) while Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure shows the banner 'No filter wheel on active profile - adaptive applies to every capture (mono camera assumption).' (siv-13-ae-on.png). Code claim is exact: adaptive_exposure_settings.dart:315-316 reads activeEquipmentProfileProvider?.filterNames; autofocus_settings.dart:128,756-760 reads filterWheelStateProvider.filterNames. I went further than the reporter: after using discovery 'Assign' to attach the wheel to the active profile (profile card then reads '1 devices', status '1 connected', sqlite equipment_profiles.filter_names still empty), the banner PERSISTS (siv-22-ae3.png) - at that point the banner's literal statement is false, because the profile does have a filter wheel. HOWEVER the strongest claim ('per-filter adaptive limits cannot be configured at all') is overstated: Equipment > Edit Profile > Filters (0 slots) > 'Auto-detect from wheel' > Save Changes writes filter_names=["L","R","G","B","Ha","OIII","SII"] and the per-filter min/max/enable editor then renders all 7 rows (siv-27-ae4.png). So this is a source-of-truth/discoverability defect with a false banner, not an unreachable feature. Severity corrected P1 -> P2.

title: 'Auto dark subtraction' in Dark Library is the same switch as 'Auto-calibrate light frames' - turning it off silently kills flat and bias correction too
what_happened: Settings > Equipment > Dark Library > 'Auto dark subtraction' ('Automatically subtract matching darks from light frames') and Settings > Equipment > Calibration > 'Auto-calibrate light frames' ('Apply dark, flat, and bias correction to captured images automatically') are one and the same setting (calibration.auto_calibrate). I switched OFF 'Auto dark subtraction' on the Dark Library page; the DB key calibration.auto_calibrate flipped true->false and the Calibration page's 'Auto-calibrate light frames' was then also OFF.
expected: A control labelled 'Auto dark subtraction' must control dark subtraction only, or be labelled to say it is the master calibration switch. As shipped, a user who wants darks off but flats on has no way to express that and is not told what they just switched off.
repro: Settings > Equipment > Calibration: turn 'Auto-calibrate light frames' ON (DB calibration.auto_calibrate=true). Settings > Equipment > Dark Library: turn 'Auto dark subtraction' OFF. sqlite3 .../skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='calibration.auto_calibrate'" -> false. Return to Calibration: 'Auto-calibrate light frames' is OFF.
proposed_fix: Either rename the Dark Library row to 'Auto-calibrate light frames (dark, flat, bias)' and mirror the Calibration subtitle verbatim, or split it into a real per-frame-type gate. Do not keep one boolean behind two contradictory labels.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Settings > Equipment > Calibration: turned 'Auto-calibrate light frames' ON -> sqlite app_settings calibration.auto_calibrate=true. Settings > Equipment > Dark Library then showed 'Auto dark subtraction' already ON (siv-30-darklib.png), i.e. one boolean behind two labels. Turned it OFF there -> calibration.auto_calibrate=false and the Calibration page's 'Auto-calibrate light frames' is OFF (siv-31-cal-after.png). Code path confirmed: dark_library_settings.dart:81-91 -> DarkLibrarySettingsActions.setAutoCalibrate (dark_library_provider.dart:357-364) -> CalibrationSettingsNotifier.setAutoCalibrate; the read at dark_library_provider.dart:322 is stored['calibration.auto_calibrate']. The consequence also holds: imaging_service.dart:582 gates the ENTIRE calibrateFile() call (which returns darkApplied/flatApplied/biasApplied) on calSettings.autoCalibrate, so switching off 'Auto dark subtraction' does disable flat and bias correction. Severity corrected P1 -> P2: nothing is lost (the uncalibrated FITS is still written and the raw frames survive); the defect is a mislabeled control that silently widens its scope.

title: File naming pattern accepts unknown variables and path-traversal segments with no validation; the failure only surfaces at capture time
what_happened: Settings > Imaging > 'File naming pattern' accepted and persisted '../../../pwned/$NOPE' and later '$TARGET_$BANANA' with no error, no warning and no preview. DB app_settings.file_naming_pattern held the literal strings. The capture pipeline rejects both: expandNamingPattern throws ValidationException for unknown tokens and buildImageFilePath throws for '..' segments - i.e. every frame of the night fails to be written, and the user is only told when the first exposure completes.
expected: Validate on commit: reject unknown $TOKENs and unsafe path segments in the settings field (the pipeline already has the token set and the segment rules), and show the resolved example filename live like NINA does.
repro: Settings > Imaging > click the 'File naming pattern' field, Ctrl+A, type '$TARGET_$BANANA', Enter. Field shows '$TARGET_$BANANA' in normal (non-error) styling. sqlite3 .../skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='file_naming_pattern'" -> $TARGET_$BANANA.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-12-pattern.png (../../../pwned/$NOPE accepted) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-115-pattern-banana.png (crop115.png); DB output 'file_naming_pattern|$TARGET_$BANANA'. NOTE: the capture-time throw was NOT observed live - desktop 'Snapshot' is preview-only (badge 'Preview only' in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-123-snap2.png, Session 'Captured 0 frames', empty /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/captures/), so triggering it needs a full sequence run which was outside this area. The throw is read at the named lines.
proposed_fix: Reuse ImagingService._patternVariables and the segment rules in a SettingsTextInput validator so the field refuses to commit an invalid pattern, and render a live 'M31/Light/M31_L_120s_0001.fits' preview under the row.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: Settings > Imaging > File naming pattern, Ctrl+A, typed '../../../pwned/$NOPE', Enter. Field renders the value in normal (non-error) styling with no warning and no preview (siv-35-pattern-bad.png); sqlite app_settings.file_naming_pattern = '../../../pwned/$NOPE'. Code claims verified: imaging_settings.dart:63-83 wires SettingsTextInput straight to setFileNamingPattern with no validator, and settings_sections/imaging.dart:36-39 persists whatever it is given. The consequence chain is real: namingPatternProvider (imaging_provider.dart:288-294) reads settings.fileNamingPattern -> _generateImageFilePath (imaging_service/file_paths.dart:50) -> buildImageFilePath, which throws ValidationException for unknown $TOKENs (imaging_service.dart ~1057-1067) and for '..'/empty/unsafe segments (~1131-1143); the comment at imaging_service.dart:400-403 states file-path failure 'fails the capture and stops loop callers'. Existing tests (imaging_service_test.dart:2479, 2500) already assert both throws. CORRECTION to the framing: there is no path traversal - the pipeline rejects '..' segments and additionally enforces path.isWithin(basePath, candidate), so 'path-traversal' overstates it. This is a deferred-error validation gap, not a security hole. Severity corrected P1 -> P2.

title: Adaptive Conditions accepts all-zero score weights and calls it a readability preference; it actually switches the feature off
what_happened: I set transparency/seeing/cloud/wind weights all to 0 (each field's min is 0, and there is no floor on the total). The page persisted {"transparency":0.0,"seeing":0.0,"cloud":0.0,"wind":0.0} and displayed: 'Weights sum to 0.00. The composer renormalizes available axes at runtime, but keeping the total near 1.00 makes the score easier to reason about.' That message is untrue for a zero total: AdaptiveSwapService.compose returns null when weightTotal <= 0, so no conditions score is ever produced and adaptive target swapping silently degrades to 'ConditionsUnknown' forever.
expected: Either refuse to commit a configuration whose total is 0, or say what actually happens: 'All weights are zero - no conditions score can be computed and adaptive swapping will not run.'
repro: Settings > Automation & Safety > Adaptive Conditions > Score weights: set each of the four fields to 0 (click, Ctrl+A, type 0, Enter).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/adaptive_conditions_settings.dart:65-68 and :271-273 (min:0, no total floor); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/adaptive_swap_service.dart:174 ('if (weightTotal <= 0) return null;')
proposed_fix: Clamp the commit so at least one weight is > 0, and change the warning copy for the zero case to state that the score cannot be computed.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Settings > Automation & Safety > Adaptive Conditions, set all four weights to 0 -> sqlite adaptive_swap.score_weights = {"transparency":0.0,"seeing":0.0,"cloud":0.0,"wind":0.0} and the callout reads exactly 'Weights sum to 0.00. The composer renormalizes available axes at runtime, but keeping the total near 1.00 makes the score easier to reason about.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-39-callout.png). Code confirmed: adaptive_conditions_settings.dart _ScoreWeightRow uses min:0 with no total floor, and _WeightTotalCallout branches only on nearOne (|total-1|<0.001) so the zero case falls into the generic 'renormalizes' copy. adaptive_swap_service.dart:174 is 'if (weightTotal <= 0) return null;' and AdaptiveSwapDriver.tick (line ~272) pushes that null straight to sequencerUpdateConditionsScore, so no conditions score ever reaches the Rust decision path (AdaptiveSwapDecision::ConditionsUnknown, adaptive_swap.rs:306/318). The copy is therefore untrue for a zero total. P2 stands - this is the 'app states something untrue' class, though it requires a deliberate all-zero config on a feature whose 'Enabled for new schedulers' toggle is off by default.

title: Sequence checkpoints and logs are written to the platform app-support directory, ignoring the configured data directory
unit: settings:captured-images (observed while auditing; owner is the sequencer/storage layer)
what_happened: With SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR both pointed at /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/data, the app logged 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' and 'Log directory: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs'. skotiq_session.checkpoint in that shared directory was being rewritten by my sandboxed instance. The visible consequence: on entering the app I was offered 'Recover Sequence? ... New Sequence, Saved 0m ago, Completed 6 frames (0m integration)' for a sequence that does not exist in this profile's database (select * from sequence_checkpoints returned zero rows).
expected: Checkpoint and log paths must follow the same data-directory resolution as the database, so a second profile/data-dir never reads or overwrites another instance's run state.
repro: Start the app with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR set to a scratch path; read /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/app.log for the two 'directory' lines; ls -la ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/ shows skotiq_session.checkpoint mtime tracking the sandboxed run.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/app.log lines at 13:54:14 ('Log directory: ...') and 13:54:15 ('Setting checkpoint directory to: ...'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-04-skip.png (the phantom Recover dialog); sqlite3 output 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> empty
where: source-only beyond the log lines - the checkpoint-directory call site is in the native bridge startup path, not in my area's Dart files
proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint and log roots from the same SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware helper the database uses.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently in my own fresh instance. /proc/1436364/environ confirms SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging-verify/data, yet that instance's own log says 'Log directory: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs' (15:10:40) and 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' (15:10:41). The visible consequence reproduced too: immediately after 'Skip onboarding' the app offered 'Recover Sequence? ... AUDIT SEQ, Saved 0m ago, Completed 2 frames' (siv-02-skip.png) for a sequence that does not exist in this profile - sqlite 'select count(*) from sequence_checkpoints' returns 0. The dialog is modal and Escape does not dismiss it, so the only exits are Resume (would run another instance's sequence) or Discard (I backed the shared file up first, clicked Discard, and restored it - which also proves the write side of the hazard). CORRECTION to the finding's 'where': the call site is NOT in the native bridge startup path, it is Dart - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 calls backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir(supportDir.path) with getApplicationSupportDirectory(), and apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60-68 pins the log dir the same way (configureSkotiqDataDirectory only fills SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when it is unset, and the logDir/checkpoint paths never consult it at all). Severity P2 stands: for a single desktop instance the practical impact is only that a relocated data directory is not honoured, but the project documents running a headless daemon alongside a GUI on one host (main_headless with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR), and in that supported configuration the two processes share one checkpoint file.
